# The conformance tests that fail when every plain build goes through the compiler in cancho (`CANCHO_COMPILER=auto`),
# each a difference from the Rust compiler and not a missing feature, measured on macOS aarch64 and Linux x86-64
# (2026-10-15). The `selfhost` job of ci.yml skips these and fails on any other. Take a line out when the difference is
# closed (`cargo test -p cancho --test conformance -- <name>` with the variable set, and it passes), and never add one
# without an issue: a new difference is a bug in `examples/selfhost` or in the Rust compiler. Tracked in #491.
checked_output::an_earlier_failure_is_still_reported_and_keeps_being_reported   # the Cranelift backend's error text; the test builds with it
corpus::accepted_programs_build_and_run                                        # compares the object bytes the Rust backends write
memory::the_layout_report_says_what_a_type_costs                               # a struct of bytes has another stride
modules::std_declarations_cost_nothing_unless_called                           # Linux only: the size of the module
wasm_target::build_refuses_too_not_only_check                                  # the WebAssembly target is the Rust compiler's (#486)
devices::a_missing_device_is_a_value_not_a_crash                                                               # the compiler in cancho writes no code for the edition-12 device verbs yet (#665); the Rust compiler does
devices::a_node_that_is_not_a_device_is_refused_when_configured                                                # the compiler in cancho writes no code for the edition-12 device verbs yet (#665); the Rust compiler does
devices::a_size_or_rate_with_no_meaning_is_refused_before_the_device_is_touched                                # the compiler in cancho writes no code for the edition-12 device verbs yet (#665); the Rust compiler does
devices::a_path_outside_the_bound_traps                                                                        # the compiler in cancho writes no code for the edition-12 device verbs yet (#665); the Rust compiler does
